_readme: THE MODEL INPUT CONTRACT — what each settled door actually accepts, in the maker's own field names, with the order the maker recommends the prompt be assembled in, and which of OUR scene/frame fields fills each field.

Written 2026-09-18 from the research notes; every row carries the doc URL it was read from. This file exists so that a scene is never assembled by guessing: run.py builds every item's fields from here, preflight.py's contract gate refuses an item that is missing one, and machine/render_model_inputs.py renders it into MODEL-INPUTS.md so a prompt can READ the contract instead of restating it.

The doors are settled (providers.json `doors`, providers/MODEL-HOUSE.md) and are not re-opened here. A station names its door; a model slug is never repeated here — `model_from` points at the place in providers.json that holds it, so there is exactly one copy of every slug in the machine.
No brand, product, person or format word appears in this file.

2026-09-22 — the clip door moved (the owner, after a live bake-off on one scene): the settled clip model takes TWO shapes, and the shape is decided by whether the scene speaks. A TALKING scene = image_references [the first frame] + audio_references [the voice slice], NO end_image; a SILENT scene = start_image + end_image, no audio. The backend's own 422, verbatim: "start_image/end_image cannot be mixed with reference media; audio_references require at least one image or video reference." So the asset line drops the @Image2 sentence on a talking scene and the last beat says in words where the clip ends; a silent scene keeps @Image2 and settles on its framing. Duration 4–15 s, 2K only.

aspect.what: declared ONCE per piece, never per scene — every still, every clip and every crop carries the same value

resolution.what: declared ONCE per piece — the still size and the clip resolution are resolved from it per station

still-generate.makes: the FIRST FRAME of a scene — a generation, because no source image exists yet. It carries its references (cast sheet, packshot, style frame) in the order the maker preserves detail in.
still-generate.endpoint_rule: a first frame always carries at least the cast sheet, so it posts to images/edits with the references as repeated image[] parts; with no reference at all it posts to images/generations

assembly.rule: the maker's own order for a photographic still — concrete over abstract, and the more specific the words, the more of the frame is decided rather than invented. This is the order a FIRST FRAME is written in, in the brief and in the prompt. `viewpoint` is present on a faceless frame (frame_rules.viewpoint) and sits right after camera.

limits.references: cast sheet first (finest detail preserved), packshot second, style frame last
limits.one_person_per_call: keep one described person per call — an edit that does not name who drifts wardrobe onto everyone
limits.text_in_frame: generate the plate clean; words go on as a layer afterwards (frames-by-edit.md)
limits.input_fidelity: REJECTED on 2.5 — invalid_input_fidelity_model, live 2026-09-18 (providers.json direct.openai.proven). It belongs to the 2.x models; do not send it on the settled slug.

fills_from_frame.subject: who is in it — by the cast name the brief already fixed, never a re-description of the face
fills_from_frame.composition: how it is framed and how much of the frame each thing occupies
fills_from_frame.action: what the person or the object is doing at this instant
fills_from_frame.location: the world block this scene plays in, by its name
fills_from_frame.camera: the result — how high, how close, how much depth — never a named device
fills_from_frame.lighting: where the light comes from and how flat it is

still-edit.makes: the scene's LAST FRAME — an EDIT of its first frame, whose prompt names ONLY the delta. An edit instruction must never describe anything the source image already shows. This is the everyday edit door (the owner 2026-09-18: cheaper, and good).

fields.name: contents[0].parts[].inline_data
fields.values: image refs, in order — the previous frame first, the cast sheet second; up to 6 object refs / 5 character refs on Pro
fields.fills: the previous frame, then the character's cast sheet

fields.name: contents[0].parts[].text
fields.values: the instruction — the delta only, stated as a verb
fields.fills: the frame's Do / Change line

fields.name: generationConfig.imageConfig.aspectRatio
fields.fills: the piece's Aspect

fields.name: generationConfig.imageConfig.imageSize
fields.fills: the piece's Resolution

assembly.rule: the whole prompt is the change, stated as a verb — add, remove, move, turn, change the grade. Nothing already visible in the source frame is mentioned. Measured: full re-description ran 4,262 characters and blended two identities; delta-only ran 204–386 and held the scene (frames-by-edit.md).
assembly.keep_line: Keep the person, wardrobe, setting, colour, white balance and light exactly as in the reference. Change nothing else.
assembly.keep_line_why: the delta says what changes; this one line says what may not. Without it an edit door re-decides the exposure, the wardrobe and the room, and the first/last pair reads as two different shots (live 2026-09-18).
assembly.keep_viewpoint_why: a camera move re-frames the hands; it never re-seats the body — the arms keep entering from the same edge (frame_rules.viewpoint)

limits.watermark: every image carries a non-removable SynthID mark
limits.delta_only: a frame whose prompt describes the room, the wardrobe or the face is re-generating, not editing — the defect this station exists to prevent
limits.references: ALWAYS TWO references, in this order: the previous frame FIRST, the character's cast sheet SECOND. Measured live 2026-09-18 — with the frame alone as the only reference the face drifted.

fills_from_frame.camera: named only when the camera itself moves on this frame
fills_from_frame.refs: inline_data — the previous frame first, then the packshot where a product reappears

still-edit.after: a mechanical colour match, every time, before the still is verified: resize the edit to the first frame's exact size, then match it per channel to the first frame by histogram (machine/colour_match.py, pure PIL). An edit door returns its own exposure and white balance, and a first/last pair that disagrees on either reads as two shots.
still-edit.status: alternate — not the ruled door since 2026-09-18 (all image work on direct:openai)

still-edit-fidelity.makes: THE FACE-RESCALE EDIT — the same delta edit at the stills door, for a last frame whose camera moves in on the face or takes a new angle on it. Measured live 2026-09-18: the edit door held the face but under-delivered the camera move; the fidelity door delivered both.

assembly.rule: the maker's own four blocks, in this order, assembled from the shared `clip_prompt` shape at the top of this file. (1) the asset line: what @Image1 and @Image2 are; (2) ONE clean summary sentence from labelled slots; (3) the timeline of beats, one verb each, spans off the one voice track, the first anchored on @Image1 and the last settling on @Image2; (4) what holds — the take, the setting, the light, the wardrobe, Nobody speaks, the negatives.

blocks.assets: @Image1 is the first frame: <the first frame in one line>. @Image2 is the last frame: <the delta as a description>.
blocks.summary: one sentence — who, where, what they do, the style, the camera
blocks.timeline: 0-2.54s: … · 3.18-4.55s: … — one verb per beat, the spans read off the one voice track, the first beat naming the frame at @Image1 and the last settling on the framing of @Image2; a silent beat may carry the words playing over it
blocks.consistency: One continuous take, no cuts, <the camera sentence>. Same <setting>, same <light>, same wardrobe throughout. No subtitles. No background music.

limits.max_beats_why: the maker's own warning: a storyboard is better suited to 15 panels or fewer; past that the order drifts and frames go still
limits.duration_note: the owner 2026-09-22: most scenes should be 4–6 seconds with a few frames/movements. A scene longer than 15 s is refused by rule 12: split at a beat, or route to the alternate door (seedance_2_5, up to 30 s)
limits.one_verb_why: two short actions are stable, three or more drift — a beat that names two actions is two beats
limits.no_high_frequency_action: timestamps do not control repeated fast motion
limits.ceilings_from: providers.json models[...].ceilings — text and labels garble, hands near a product merge, a product label must be reference-locked
limits.frames_per_scene_why: first and last only — the beats between them are written into the timeline, never generated as stills
limits.clip_media_roles_why: EXACTLY these roles on a silent clip, and nothing else — the first frame as start_image, the last as end_image, no audio. A cast sheet or a style frame beside them is a second opinion about the same face, and the dry run that found this bug had sent both instead of the first frame (2026-09-18).
limits.duration_from: ceil(the scene's slice of the voice track), floored at the door's minimum (4). The ceiling (15) is NOT clamped — a paragraph past it is refused by name so the scene is split at a beat boundary or routed to the alternate door, never quietly shortened.
limits.no_end_image_with_audio_why: the backend's 422, verbatim: "start_image/end_image cannot be mixed with reference media; audio_references require at least one image or video reference."

voice.makes: ONE continuous track for the whole piece — every scene's paragraph spoken in order, stitched request to request so the read never restarts, then sliced per scene for the talking door

fields.name: text
fields.fills: the scene's Voice paragraph, byte-identical to the script

fields.name: model_id
fields.note: eleven_v3 is the house voice model since 2026-10-01 (the owner: "just use whatever is the best thing for voice … clean and clear … consistent"): measured on the Nova read, Multilingual v2 let a designed voice drift to Australian on 3–4 of 4 listens; v3 held General American 4 of 4. v3 does not take request stitching, so each line is read on its own (voice.py stitches() skips it) and stability is snapped to 0 / 0.5 / 1 (for_model).

fields.name: previous_request_ids
fields.values: the request ids of the up-to-3 most recent chunks, read from each response's `request-id` header
fields.fills: the scene order — this is what makes one read instead of many
fields.note: conditions on the audio actually generated, not just the neighbouring words; it overrides previous_text when both are sent; ids expire after 2 hours

fields.name: previous_text / next_text
fields.note: ignored when previous_request_ids is sent — the machine sends the ids

fields.name: voice_settings
fields.fills: the character's own voice record

fields.name: apply_text_normalization
fields.fills: pinned — machine/spoken_numbers.py has already said every figure in words (spoken-rules.json), so ElevenLabs' own guess is switched off
fields.note: read 2026-09-23: 'three modes: auto, on, off', default auto, no model restriction stated for eleven_multilingual_v2. Pinned by the owner's 2026-09-23 ask: numbers said one known way

fields.name: seed
fields.fills: pinned — every chunk of a read sends the same seed; a remake of a scene sends seed + the remake number, recorded in timing.json
fields.note: read 2026-09-23: 'best effort to sample deterministically, such that repeated requests with the same seed and parameters should return the same result' — best effort, not a guarantee

fields.name: pronunciation_dictionary_locators
fields.values: dictionary id + version on the ElevenLabs account
fields.fills: — not used: the brand's protected words are swapped into the text before the call (machine/lexicon.py, brands/<brand>/brand-identity/voice/pronunciation.json)
fields.note: phoneme (IPA) rules only work on eleven_flash_v2 and eleven_v3, not eleven_multilingual_v2; alias rules work everywhere but live on the account where the team cannot see them, and the music door takes no dictionary — so the swap is ours, in the text, visible in a file

returns.alignment: {characters, character_start_times_seconds, character_end_times_seconds} against the raw text
returns.normalized_alignment: the same shape against the normalised text
returns.request-id: an HTTP response header — carried into the next chunk's previous_request_ids

assembly.rule: one chunk per scene paragraph — never per sentence. Shooting line by line is what made the read choppy; the paragraph is the unit, and the stitch carries the read across scene boundaries.

limits.chunking: the API does not chunk — the machine picks the boundaries, and the boundary is the scene

fills_from_frame.scene_slice: vo/<scene>.mp3, cut from the one track at the scene's own start and end

pins._why: the owner, 2026-09-23: numbers and brand words said one known way. The text is prepared by lexicon.for_model (protected words → say_as, then spoken_numbers) before every chunk; these two pins make that preparation the only decider and the take repeatable

sfx-generate.makes: ONE row of the SFX bank (tools/video-production/banks/sfx) — a cue or a room-tone bed, made once and reused forever. machine/make_bank.py builds the call from the row; --dry-run only until a spend is approved (2026-09-23).

fields.name: text
fields.fills: the bank row's `prompt`

fields.name: duration_seconds
fields.fills: the bank row's `seconds`

fields.name: loop
fields.fills: the bank row's `loop` — true on every room-tone bed

assembly.rule: The row's prompt, verbatim. Nothing else is written into it.

music-compose.makes: ONE row of the music bank (tools/video-production/banks/music) — an instrumental bed tagged energy · tempo · mood, made once and reused forever. machine/make_bank.py builds the call from the row; --dry-run only until a spend is approved (2026-09-23).

fields.name: prompt
fields.fills: the bank row's `prompt` (energy, mood and BPM written into it)

fields.name: music_length_ms
fields.fills: the bank row's `seconds` × 1000

fields.name: force_instrumental
fields.fills: — a bed sits under a voice; it never sings

assembly.rule: The row's prompt, verbatim. Never a named commercial track.

door_of_registry._readme: providers.json's own door name for a station -> the door row in this file. The registry decides WHICH door a run uses; this file says what that door takes. A door the registry names and this map does not know falls back to the station's preferred_door, and the submit sheet says which was used.

edit_routing._readme: Which door an edit goes to. the owner, 2026-09-18: 'we'll just do gpt for all image work both initial reference gen and edits' — EVERY edit goes to the fidelity door (direct:openai images/edits, input_fidelity high, two references). The camera word on a LAST FRAME block (same · push-in · new angle) is still declared, for the director and the record, but it no longer changes the door.

all_edits.why: one image door for generation and edits; measured 2026-09-18 on one scene: the fidelity edit held the face and landed the push-in with two references + colour match

alternate.when: only if the registry's edit door is flipped back to direct:google
alternate.why: cheaper per call; held the face with the cast sheet as a second reference but under-delivered the camera move

aspect_words._readme: the framing sentence appended to every FIRST FRAME prompt — the piece's Aspect said in words, because a size parameter alone does not tell the door how to compose the frame

_readme: THE FOUR BLOCKS — the shape of the call that worked live on 2026-09-18 evening (first frame + last frame + the scene's voice slice, 9 s, line check 100%), carried to the settled clip door on 2026-09-22 (the bake-off: line check 95%, words identical, face held, lip sync good).
Every block is built from LABELLED fields. A slot that resolves to nothing is a refusal by name, never a fragment: nothing submits red, so a prompt that cannot be built is not written at all.

Both clip stations (motion and talking) use this one shape. The differences: a TALKING scene has an @Audio1 sentence, no @Image2 sentence, a last beat that ENDS ON the LAST FRAME's Change in words, and the lip line; a SILENT scene has an @Image2 sentence, the words playing over each beat, a last beat settling on the framing of @Image2, and 'Nobody speaks.' Each names the condition it appears under.

assets.audio: @Audio1 is {who}'s voice; they speak the words in @Audio1 exactly, their lips moving with every word, nothing else is said.
assets.audio_when: a to-camera scene only — the slice is attached as audio_references, and the first frame beside it as image_references
assets.last_when: a silent scene only — a talking scene on the settled door attaches no end_image (start_image/end_image cannot be mixed with reference media), so @Image2 is not on the call and the sentence is dropped; the last beat says where the clip ends instead

summary.rule: ONE clean sentence, assembled from labelled slots and never by gluing raw fields end to end. A missing slot is a refusal.

who.what: who is in it, as the brief describes them

setting.what: the one world block the scene plays in

does.what: what they do — the scene's own outcome/section line, never a paraphrase of the paragraph

style.what: the style words, declared once for the piece by the format profile

camera.what: the camera in one phrase, built from the LAST FRAME's Camera word and the FIRST FRAME's Composition

timeline.words_when: a silent scene only — a to-camera scene carries its words as attached audio, and writing them twice is how a clip ends up saying something else
timeline.last_beat_when: a scene whose last frame is attached (a silent scene on the settled door; any scene on the alternate)
timeline.last_beat_talking_when: a scene whose last frame is NOT attached — a talking scene on the settled door: the LAST FRAME's Change, said in words, is where the clip ends
timeline.rule: one verb a beat, the spans read off the one voice track, the first beat anchored on @Image1 and the last landing on @Image2 where it is attached — or, where it is not, ending on the LAST FRAME's Change in words.

consistency.lip: The speaker is talking for the whole clip: their lips, jaw and face move naturally with the voice throughout.
negatives: No subtitles, no captions, no on-screen text.
consistency.silent_when: a B-roll scene only — the voice plays OVER it at the edit, so the clip itself carries no speech and no mouth moves in it
consistency.hold_clause_rule: THE HOLD SENTENCE IS WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, so a clause of the FIRST FRAME's Lighting that a BEAT changes is dropped from it and named on the record. Live 2026-09-22: the first frame's lighting ended 'no practicals, no fill, no running water' — a true description of the frame — and the consistency block then told the clip 'same … no running water … throughout' while beat 4 said 'moves the hand under the running tap'. The clip did what both said: the tap ran with no one turning it on (the owner: 'the water just magically turned on'). A lighting clause names the LIGHT; a clause about what is or is not happening in the frame belongs to the first frame alone.
consistency.hold_drop_when: the clause's own subject is named by any beat's `do`

camera_phrases.new angle: one move to a new angle, {target}

camera_sentences.push-in: the only camera movement is the slow push in
camera_sentences.new angle: the only camera movement is the one move onto the new angle
camera_sentences.pull-out: the only camera movement is the slow pull out

clip_prompt.camera_target: the words after 'to' on the LAST FRAME's Camera line — `push-in to close`. A move that names no framing to land on is a refusal, never a guess.
clip_prompt.first_framing: the FIRST FRAME's Composition up to its first comma — the framing the move starts from.
clip_prompt.camera_words_why: EXACTLY these four, and a move always names the framing it lands on, in the same words the FIRST FRAME's Composition uses. 'new angle' alone is a move with nowhere to go, and the gate refuses it by name rather than guessing.

_readme: A beat is ONE visible action, one verb, present tense, something a camera can see. How a line is delivered is not an action: it belongs in the bracket at the end of the beat, never in Do.
Two actions joined by 'and', 'then' or a comma are two beats. A pause is a beat whose action is `holds`, with the pause in Over.
beat_grammar.delivery_verbs_why: the verb a beat opens on is what the camera sees happen. These name how the line is performed, not what moves — they belong in the bracket.
beat_grammar.pause_why: a pause IS a beat: `Do: holds`, with the silence named in Over. It is the one beat whose action is stillness, and it is never a delivery note.
beat_grammar.insert_why: B-ROLL IS A SCENE, NOT AN INSERT (2026-09-19). Where the argument shows something, the brief writes a scene of its own — `to_camera: false`, its own setting, frames, beats and the paragraph that plays over it. An insert wedged inside another scene's beat is a second picture inside one clip, and one clip cannot cut.

to_camera_hold.rule: On a to-camera scene a beat whose action is the pause verb does not read as 'holds' — a held face with audio attached came back with the mouth barely moving (live 2026-09-19, scene 1). It reads as: talks to the lens, the mouth moving with every word{, plus the bracket}.
to_camera_hold.text: talks to the lens, the mouth moving with every word

door_rules._readme: Per clip slug, what rule 12 says when a scene does not fit the door — keyed by the slug providers.json names, so the one slug the registry holds is the one this looks up. A slug with no row here gets the generic refusal.

minimax_h3.over_ceiling: split at a beat, or route to the alternate door (seedance_2_5, up to 30 s)
minimax_h3.no_end_image_with_audio: the backend's 422, verbatim: "start_image/end_image cannot be mixed with reference media; audio_references require at least one image or video reference." — a talking scene attaches image_references + audio_references and no end_image; a silent scene attaches start_image + end_image and no audio
minimax_h3.resolution: 2K only — the piece's Resolution sizes the stills; the clip is 2K

_readme: THE BRIEF IS THE PROMPT (the owner, 2026-09-19: "this brief is for the AI system to interpret, not for me as the human to read — format these briefs in a way that AI is able to directly build what it needs to build").

So the truth of a brief is the LAST fenced json block in it, in this shape. The Markdown above the block is the readable view for a person, rendered from these same fields; nothing downstream parses it.

Every key below is present on every object — a string stays a string, a list stays a list, and a key with nothing to say carries an empty string rather than being dropped. A dropped key is a gap the gate cannot tell from an omission.
brief_schema.may_be_empty_why: a key that is PRESENT and says nothing — a character who never speaks has no voice id, a beat where the camera does not move has no camera word, a scene with no caption has no on-screen text. Every other key carries something or the brief is not finished.

optional.why: Present where the brief has something to say and absent where it does not — never required, and never a refusal. `openings` carries the hook set, which is a test rather than a scene; `style` is the one grade sentence, taken from the first scene's frame when the piece does not state it; `held` is the one fact that would release a scene the brand's own files cannot fill; `happens` is what the scene DOES in one verb phrase, which is the one slot of the clip's summary sentence a frame field reads badly for. `voice_settings` is the spoken pass's per-scene voice-model settings (stability · style · speed, inside the register recipe's range in components/marketing-doctrine/spoken.json), laid over the cast voice's own record for that chunk; absent, the cast record alone speaks. `viewpoint` is optional on a frame with a face in it and REQUIRED on a frame with none (see rules). `edit` is the brief's notes for the edit (captions, music, effects). `roll_sheet` is the carried-or-dropped table (v13, 2026-09-23): absent on a brief written before it, which is WARNED, never refused.
optional.why_elements: ELEMENTS.md §1–4 (2026-09-23): `opens` (true on the scroll-stopper) and `priority` (1 = never cut) on a scene; `layers`, `music`, `sfx` and `hooks` on the brief. Production carries them into plan.json untouched for the edit, and resolves music and sfx to bank rows. Absent is fine; present and malformed is a gate finding naming the field. A scene's `section` (required) is a section id from components/marketing-doctrine/frameworks.json and the piece's `framework` an id from components/marketing-doctrine/ad-frameworks.json, or `observed — <a plain description>` — both READ from the doctrine at run time, never listed here (2026-09-23, brief v15); a value off either list is a gate finding naming the real ids. v14's `module` is retired: read only as a deprecated alias for a missing `section`, with a warning (see elements.module_deprecated).

rules: every scene has at least one beat and a voice paragraph — a to-camera scene's paragraph is spoken, a B-roll scene's is the voice playing over it
a scene with to_camera false is B-roll: the clip carries no audio, and its paragraph is laid under it at the edit
setting_id names a world block that exists in world[]
the last frame's camera is one of the four phrases, and a move names the framing it lands on
one verb per beat, present tense, visible — never a delivery note

a scene carrying `held` is a scene nothing can make yet: it keeps its place and its section, it names the one fact that would release it, and the machine builds nothing for it rather than generating a frame nobody can describe
the piece's aspect_ratio and resolution are values the doors take — a ratio and one of the clip door's own words, never a pixel pair

a scene's `voice` is SPOKEN copy, read aloud by the voice model exactly as written, ONE THOUGHT PER BREATH (the owner, 2026-09-19): no em-dash or en-dash, no semicolon, no parenthesis or bracket. An ellipsis (...) is the mid-thought breath and is KEPT — never a chop into short statements; a full stop ends a thought; an exclamation or question lifts it. The dash/semicolon/parenthesis are read as long silences or the wrong shape and the gate refuses them by name

a frame with NO FACE in it — hands, the product, a body part — carries a `viewpoint`: whose eyes the camera is, and which edge of the frame EVERY limb enters from, with elbows off-frame. Without it the image door invents the body: live 2026-09-22 the left arm dropped in from the top-left corner and the right hand came up from the bottom-right, two arms no one body could own (the owner: "tell me how this angle makes sense, the arms are so odd"). The gate refuses a faceless first frame with no viewpoint by name

every scene carries `to_camera` as true or false — never omitted. A scene without it is refused by id before anything is made: the machine never guesses whether a scene is the speaker or B-roll (the owner, 2026-09-23 — a missing value used to default to a talking scene, which is how a B-roll shot silently became a face)

a card is a scene of `kind: "card"` (the owner, 2026-09-23: cards are made at production, not left for the edit). It carries a `plate` — the picture with NO words in it — which is made as ONE still and no clip, and its exact words as `lines`, with `lands_on` and `sfx`, which travel to the edit as data (`scene.card` in plan.json). Type is a layer, never a generation: a plate with quoted words or a card line in it is refused. A card line with `[UNFILLED]` is warned — the figure is not settled in the offer file

`roll_sheet` maps every row of the swipe's make-list to a scene id of the matching kind (a B-over / B-vo / B-silent row to a to_camera:false scene that is not a card, a C row to a card scene) or to a reason in `dropped`. A row with neither, or pointing at a scene that does not exist or is the wrong kind, stops the run before anything is made, named by its row. A brief with no roll sheet at all is older and is warned, never refused

voice_forbidden._why: the owner, 2026-09-19: 'humans don't use em dashes when speaking'. These marks are writing, not speech. The voice model reads a dash as a long silence and a parenthesis as an aside nobody hears. The spoken script (stage 4g) writes the paragraph without them; this list is what the gate checks, and voice.py's for_reading() keeps a safety net for older briefs.

marks.name: spaced hyphen used as a dash

voice_forbidden.map_from: components/marketing-doctrine/spoken.json → punctuation_map (the same marks, with what each does on the voice model)

voice_settings_ranges._why: the voice-settings guide's own limits — speed 0.7 to 1.2, the rest 0 to 1. A value outside them is a typo the gate names rather than a call that comes back refused

voice_kept.ellipsis: '...' and '…' are KEPT: the mid-thought breath (the owner's ruling 2026-09-19, spoken.json the_thought). voice.py reads them as a short weighted pause, never replaces them.

brief_schema.kinds_why: ELEMENTS.md §1 and the AI brief v14 (2026-09-23). Every scene names its `kind`: talking (to_camera true) · broll (to_camera false) · card · screen · split · greenscreen · endcard — a kind that disagrees with to_camera is refused by id. A card's fields sit flat on the scene (v13) or nested as `card: {...}`; the four new kinds nest theirs under the kind's own name (`screen: {plate, surface, lines, lands_on}`), and flat is read the same. A screen and an endcard are ONE still and no clip; a split is two B-roll pictures (`left` and `right`, each first_frame · beats · last_frame); a GREENSCREEN IS A TALKING SCENE (to_camera true, its own frames, beats and voice) plus `greenscreen: {background, talker_scene, layout}` — talker_scene names a to_camera scene, usually itself. Type is a layer, never a generation: no plate, background or split side carries quoted words or one of its lines. An endcard's plate is an EDIT of the brand's REAL packshot (brands/<brand>/products/images.json, else products/<product>/images) — the product is `endcard.product` when the brief names it, else the one brand product its refs, plate or product_lock name; never a product generated from words. Every offer_line and a non-empty guarantee is read from brands/<brand>/products/offer-bank.md or carries [UNFILLED].

viewpoint.required_when: the scene's `to_camera` is false AND the first frame shows no face (its `who` names hands / the product, or its subject says no face)
viewpoint.says: whose eyes the camera is + which frame edge every limb enters from + elbows off-frame
viewpoint.example: Her own point of view: the camera is where her eyes are, looking down. Both forearms enter from the bottom edge of the frame, elbows out of frame, angled slightly toward the basin. No arm enters from any other edge.
viewpoint.kept_on_edit: the last frame is an edit of the first and the edit prompt repeats the viewpoint as a keep line — a camera move re-frames, it never re-seats the body
viewpoint.why: the body geometry is the one thing a still description leaves to chance when there is no face to anchor it; said in words it is decided, not invented (live 2026-09-22)

first_instant.says: This picture is the first instant only: anything the scene does later, such as a hand that comes in on a later line, is not in it yet.
first_instant.why: the three-doctors run QC, 2026-10-02: the opening still read the scene's later movement ('her right hand entering … on the second line') as already done, so the hand was up at her collar in the first frame.

wardrobe_in_words.applies_to: every still with a person who wears a named look
wardrobe_in_words.says: {who} wears {outfit} ({continuity}), exactly as in the outfit reference — their face reference is for the face only, not the clothes.
wardrobe_in_words.from: the person's own looks.json in the casting bank (outfit, continuity) — machine/element_refs.py wardrobe_words
wardrobe_in_words.why: the three-doctors run QC, 2026-10-02: with only the look sheet attached, 8 of 22 pictures put Nova in her master photo's plain T-shirt instead of the scene's look.

product_label.applies_to: every still that carries the real packshot
product_label.says: The product's label reads exactly as the packshot, letter for letter: {label_lock}.
product_label.why: the three-doctors run QC, 2026-10-02: a tube came back labelled 'PASHIDA'.

endcard.applies_to: an endcard showing more than one person
endcard.says: Equal panels, one person per panel, each exactly the same width; each person in their own place from the ad, never one shared room; the top fifth of the picture left as calm plain background for the words set in the edit; every face inside the middle 4:5 area.
endcard.why: the three-doctors run QC, 2026-10-02: the three-doctor endcard came back with a wider middle panel, all three in one generic room, and its word band outside the 4:5 zone.

swipe_camera.applies_to: every first frame, card plate or own picture that copies a swipe shot
swipe_camera.says: The FIRST reference image is the swipe shot this picture copies, blurred on purpose. Copy from it exactly: where the camera is, its height and angle, how close it is, the framing and crop, where each person and hand sits in the frame, where the light comes from, how hard or soft it is and its colour, the shading and shadows it throws on faces, necks, hands and clothes, how bright the picture is, and its camera look. Where any position written above disagrees with it, the swipe shot wins. Take nothing else from it: the people, faces, clothes, words and room details come from the other references and the words above.
swipe_camera.from: the teardown's frame map: framemap/shots/<K> usable frame, blurred to <K>-camera.jpg — machine/storyboard_plan.py with_swipe_camera puts it first on the ruled still door (GPT Image 2.5)
swipe_camera.why: the owner, 2026-10-02: 'literally look like the swipe … this is what makes it indistinguishable from AI'. THE RECIPE he confirmed the same day ('literally everything looks perfect now. Even the dark spots are on the right side of her face'): GPT Image 2.5 — the ruled still model — with this blurred shot first and the written framing dropped. A switch to Nano Banana Pro with a sharp guide and a face pass, made by a session without his ruling, came out wider, posed and pasted-in; it is withdrawn. Shadows added the same day — the owner: 'we're now missing some of the shading and shadows that are present in the actual swipe shot … we need to account for all these little things'. 'Camera look', not 'phone-camera look': the look is the swipe's own, real or stylised.

face_check.applies_to: every still with one of our people in it — a CHECK only, it changes nothing
face_check.says: Image 1 is the REFERENCE photo of one person. Image 2 is a picture we made. Find the person in image 2 who is meant to be this person (same gender, the role they play). Is it the SAME individual as image 1? Compare feature by feature: face shape and length, eye shape and colour, nose bridge and tip, lips, jawline and chin, hairline, hair colour, length and parting, and age. Clothes, light, angle and expression do not matter. Be strict: her own family must be certain it is her. If ANY feature is noticeably different, or it only looks like the same type of person, the answer is DIFFERENT. If this person is not in image 2 at all, answer ABSENT. Answer JSON only: {"verdict": "SAME" | "DIFFERENT" | "ABSENT", "why": "one short sentence"}
face_check.from: machine/identity.py check — three asks, the majority wins; filed on the picture's record and in the picture review
face_check.why: the same ruling: nothing reaches the owner with a made-up person in it.

product_scale.applies_to: every still that carries the real packshot
product_scale.says: The product is its real size and shape: exactly the packshot's proportions, and as big against the hand and face as a real one is — a hand-held product sits inside one hand and is never larger than the hand holding it, the same size as in the ad's other pictures. In a close-up the camera moves closer; the product does not grow.
product_scale.from: machine/element_refs.py, beside product_label — every still with the real packshot
product_scale.why: the owner, 2026-10-02, Round 1: Section 21's tube came out wider than her palm and nearly hand-length — 'that bottle size is not correct … compare against all the other face scrub bottles used in the generation, and also look at the actual pack shot'. Only the label was ruled; nothing ruled the size.

first_frame_kept.applies_to: every clip that starts from an approved picture
first_frame_kept.says: @Image1 is the first frame. Keep it exactly as it is: the same framing and distance from the lens, the same people, faces, clothes, place, signs and light. Nothing in it is re-staged, re-framed or zoomed.
first_frame_kept.why: 2026-10-02, Nova Section 1: the clip prompt restated the brief's framing ('close-up', 'a blank lettering band') over the approved picture; Seedance followed the words and zoomed in. The picture carries the composition; the words carry only what changes (the same rule as pictures, where the swipe shot carries the camera and the written composition is dropped).

swipe_motion.applies_to: a clip of a section the storyboard makes by motion transfer (the swipe's own movement). On the ruled route (Omni on fal, providers.json direct.omni_route, 2026-10-03) only a clip with NOBODY OF OURS ON SCREEN gets the blurred footage: a person on screen is image-to-video from the approved picture, the movement said in words, and every clip of the section starts from the approved picture, never a clip's last frame (ruling_2026_10_03_no_handoffs). The @Video1 wording below is the legacy door's (clips_plan.py, --legacy-clips)
swipe_motion.says: @Video1 is a blurred clip used ONLY for movement: copy how the camera moves (a handheld phone drifting and bobbing with the arm that holds it, or a held tripod frame, exactly as it moves there), how every person and hand moves, where each touch lands, and the timing and rhythm of each movement. Take nothing else from @Video1: no person, face, hair, clothes, sign, words, captions or place from it; everything you see comes from @Image1 and the words above.
swipe_motion.camera_phrase: the camera moving only as it does in @Video1
swipe_motion.camera_sentence: the camera moves only as it does in @Video1
swipe_motion.from: the teardown's frame map: framemap/shots/<K>.mp4, the shots of the clip's span joined in order — machine/clips_plan.py attaches it as video_references on the ruled clip door
swipe_motion.why: the storyboard's motion-transfer sections (storyboard_plan.MAKERS 'B-over'): 'the swipe's own clip drives the movement, rebuilt with our people, look and place from the locked elements and our start frame'. The same recipe as swipe_camera for pictures: the swipe carries the material, our references carry the people.

card_plate._readme: THE CARD PLATE (the owner, 2026-09-23: B-roll and cards are made at production; the edit only composes type). A card scene becomes ONE still on the still-generate door and no clip. Its prompt is the brief's `plate` sentence, the piece's grade, this clean line, then the aspect words. The card's words never enter the prompt — they travel in plan.json as scene.card and the edit sets them on the plate.
card_plate.clean_line: No added text anywhere in the picture: no words, letters, numbers, prices or captions laid over it, and clear empty space left where the words will be set later. Any printed label on a real product stays exactly as its reference shows it. The plate's surface (a receipt, a screen, a page) is framed exactly as the swipe's own card is, and nothing holds it — no hand, no fingers, no person — unless the brief's plate sentence says so. Natural colour, never posterised.
card_plate.why_surface: the three-doctors run QC, 2026-10-02: both receipt cards came back as a small receipt held in a hand, one posterised into psychedelic colour; the swipe's receipt fills the frame. Framing follows the swipe's card (2026-10-02 QC: the swipe's receipt is a strip across the middle with black above and below).

elements._readme: The enums of ELEMENTS.md, read by the production gate (model_inputs.element_faults). A value off these lists is a finding naming the field — ELEMENTS.md is the contract; change it there first, then here.

module_deprecated._readme: RETIRED 2026-09-23 (brief v15). v14 tagged each scene with a six-word `module` that restated the marketing doctrine's sections in a second, coarser vocabulary. The swap unit is now the scene's `section` — a doctrine section id, read from components/marketing-doctrine/frameworks.json at run time. A brief that still carries `module` is read with a warning: the value fills a MISSING `section` (these two renamed, every other value as itself) and is otherwise ignored. It is never checked against a list of its own.

screen.needs: one still — the screen with its words left blank; the edit sets the legible text

greenscreen.needs: one still — the background plate; the presenter is the talker scene, composited at the edit

endcard.needs: one edit of the brand's REAL packshot — never a product generated from words; the edit sets the offer lines

elements.endcard_keep_line: The product is exactly the one in the reference photograph: the same shape, the same label, the same colours and the same printed words on it, nothing redrawn, re-lettered or restyled. Only what is around it changes.
